_about: Every statement the app makes about the Claude app, Claude Code and where a chat runs: what each surface can do, how to reach it, and how a cloud task is made from a computer. Messages read their words from here (tools/claude_surfaces.py say), docs carry them in marked blocks (sync-docs), and tests/test_claude_surfaces.py fails on a statement outside it. Each entry is dated and sourced; `watch` (the maintainer's, run by .github/workflows/claude-surfaces-watch.yml in the app only) checks each quote is still on its page and flags entries after a new Claude Code release. A path a person follows is written as a destination or as numbered steps and never tells them to press, click, tap or find anything; the day it was checked and its official page are for Claude (`source`), never the person.

entries.claim: A chat on the person's own computer runs in the Claude desktop app's Code tab, with Local chosen under the message box and a folder opened beside it. The desktop app includes Claude Code, so nothing else needs installing for it, and it needs a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan. Its mode selector, in the row under the message box, offers Auto where auto mode is available, which runs without routine prompts. A new empty folder is enough: the chat makes the person's copy there itself (COMPUTER.md), and where the copy already holds a profile it sets nothing up again and asks nothing. The steps are the same on a Mac and on Windows.

If the mode menu under the message box offers Auto, choose it: Claude then asks you far less.
Paste this there: Open my job search on this computer. My copy is {copy}. Follow github.com/aranculleton/last-job-search/blob/master/COMPUTER.md
